brief:
An Israeli government without Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu may be within reach, but replacing his political ideology remains uncertain, Al Jazeera English reported. The Eisenkot bloc, led by former military chief Gadi Eisenkot, presents itself as a less right-wing option, yet questions persist about how substantially it would diverge from Netanyahu's policies on core issues.

The distinction between removing Netanyahu personally and dismantling his political approach reflects deeper divisions within Israeli politics. Even if the opposition secures enough seats to form a government, the resulting coalition may retain much of the rightward trajectory that has defined Israeli policy under Netanyahu's tenure.
dek: An Israeli government without PM Netanyahu may be close, but a government without his politics is far less certain.
title: Israeli opposition bloc offers rightward alternative to Netanyahu
